mapping_status: Extraction mapping matches the committed assets job; test-only mapped assertions, not ingestion or lexical hash proof
revision_policy: Committed assets storage uses the 64-character public payload SHA256 as source_revision. Projection fixtures use that hash, 6-digit receipt ids and 4-digit entity ids.
selection_policy: Keep existing per-stat/per-condition source selection unchanged.
Order cost, descriptions, upgrade-tier assertions, nonzero or nonnumeric nonidentity values, names, zero nonidentity values, then redundant identity metadata.
Break ties by display_order, unchanged stat_key, complete condition, then assertion id.

No fact row cap. Prefix facts use at most 14000 PostgreSQL JSON bytes, reduced by the exact identity/link shell to keep the whole card at most 15000 bytes. Existing links remain capped at 8 rows and 3500 bytes.

Additionally charge each fact's serialized receipt id and the exact wrapped-card ToolResult shell with an escaped 512-byte call id and conservative longer tool name. That envelope budget is 16384 PostgreSQL JSON bytes; duplicate evidence ids are conservatively charged again. The independent consumer still enforces its final bound.

The 757-record client-6774 catalog has its largest inspected essential projection in ability_necro_gravestone (47 essential/71 mapped assertions). Sleep Dagger has 22 essential/45 mapped assertions; Toxic Bullets has 16 essential/31 mapped assertions. Size calibration includes the committed job's 64-character source_revision, not a short synthetic label.
Every omitted selected assertion is counted explicitly; canonical facts, source keys, conditions and citations are never rewritten or dropped.
